context: Switching focus from spire-loom code generation to foundframe core domain work. This is a CRITICAL transition point where we've completed entity metadata system but paused event router treadle to align core domain first.

reentry_instructions.state_of_mind: I was deep in the spire-loom machinery, understanding how the treadle-kit works, how custom treadles can be written in workspace (o19/loom/treadles/) without modifying spire-loom package, and how EJS templates generate Rust code. I had just realized the DbEventRouterTreadle pattern and was excited about it, but wisely paused to align foundframe core first.
reentry_instructions.critical_insight: The db-event-router is NOT a general spire-loom feature - it's a foundframe-specific custom treadle that belongs in workspace. This is an important architectural boundary: general framework vs specific application logic.

big_picture.description: foundframe is a core (domain) described in terms of Managements. spire-loom uses this core to spiral out additional things (android service, client, etc.). The flow is: describe core → WARP tells what to make → spire-loom weaves spires.

patterns.current: spiral patterns - core spreading and layering (not duplication!)
patterns.future: fractal patterns - core becomes Erlang-style VM where each Management is an actor/process

spire_loom_machinery_deep_dive.description: I finally understood the full machinery pipeline

components.reed: Workspace discovery - finds packages, reads spire.yaml
components.heddles: Pattern matching - matches methods/entities to tieups
components.bobbin: Templates - EJS templates for code generation
components.shuttle: File operations - actually writes generated files
components.treadles: Generation phases - Core, Platform, DDD, etc.
